Alex: Hey folks — running into a weird TS + ESM issue when trying the edge sample app. Builds fine in Node but fails for edge bundle with these errors: TS2345 on generics and an ambiguous overload calling `client.generate()`.
Maria: can you paste the error and tsconfig? sometimes moduleResolution or lib settings bite on edge bundlers.
Alex: sure — main errors: `Argument of type 'unknown' is not assignable to parameter of type 'T'.` and `No overload matches this call`.
Alex: tsconfig has `"module": "esnext", "target": "es2022", "moduleResolution": "bundler", "noImplicitAny": true`.
Sam: bundler resolution is flaky for some packagers. Also note ESM export/conditional exports in the SDK can make type-only import paths differ between CJS/ESM which confuses TS when `allowJs` or `skipLibCheck` are off.
Ben: we've seen that — the SDK's conditional `exports` means `require('redwood-sdk')` pulls CJS which has slightly different `.d.ts` entry points. Edge sample uses `import ... from` though.
Olivia: also auth/retry behaviour on edge is different — fetch in edge doesn't expose `signal` the same way and our retry wrapper assumes `request.destroy()` on errors in Node. That matches in e2e? dev-bot: CI pipeline failed for `sdk-edge-ts` on linux — https://ci.internal/12345 (failed tests: types / bundling)
Maria: quick workaround: set `moduleResolution` to `node16` or `nodeNext` and add `skipLibCheck: true` to unblock local dev. But we should ship proper typings.
Alex: adding `skipLibCheck` helps, but still runtime fails in Edge with `TypeError: client.create is not a function` — suspect ESM default interop mismatch.
Sam: try changing default export to named exports in your sample: `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'` — that avoids default vs default-interop issues.
Alex: good tip, that fixed the runtime error but TS generic inference still fails for `client.chat<T>` where T should be typed shape of tool result.
Maria: idea: change public overloads to accept `unknown` in the generic constrained position, then expose utility type `InferResponse<T>` so users can opt in. `unknown` is safer and forces explicit casts.
Ben: downside: too many `unknown` will make DX worse for beginners. Maybe we keep `any` in overloads but make `strict` builds use a stricter definition path via `types/strict.d.ts`.
Olivia: and add small test matrix: Node (CJS/ESM), Edge (esbuild/tsup), and TS strict mode. Add sample app for each combination.
Sam: pro tip for sample apps: include a minimal `tsconfig.edge.json` with `module":"esnext","moduleResolution":"bundler","lib":["es2022","dom"],"skipLibCheck":true` and a README with `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'` usage.
Alex: posting a tiny repro here:
```
// repro.ts
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new RedwoodClient();
const res = await client.chat<{ foo: string }>("hello");
console.log(res.foo);
```
Sam: when the bundler rewrites imports, the generic param gets erased if TS can't resolve the type for the method overloads — adding an explicit type argument on the call sometimes helps but it's not great.
Maria: action items:
- Ben: investigate conditional exports + .d.ts entry points, make a stable `types/edge/index.d.ts` that bundlers pick up (owner: Ben)
- Sam: add CI matrix for edge ESM/CJS + ts strict (owner: Sam)
- Olivia: enumerate auth/retry behavior differences and add polyfills/guards in our retry wrapper for fetch on edge (owner: Olivia)
- Alex: add minimal sample repro to `examples/sdk-edge-ts` with recommended tsconfig (owner: Alex)
Ben: I'll also prototype an alternative overload pattern that prefers developer ergonomics but preserves strict-compat via a boolean generic or helper types.
Alex: thanks. tagging @maria for types review once Ben has a PR. :thumbsup:
dev-bot: created issue RED-789: "SDK: edge typings + ESM/CJS parity + auth retry mismatch" — https://issues.internal/RED-789
Maria: sounds good. if anyone hits this in the wild ping #devex and drop repro. small, reproducible samples help a lot.
Olivia: I'll try to write a deterministic test for the retry differences tomorrow and post results.
Sam: noted. will scaffold CI jobs and include node:16/18, ts:4.9/5.1 matrix.
Alex: thanks team — will push the example later today and link here.
